source.title: UpSafe°C: Upcycling for Controllable Safety in Large Language Models
source.authors: Yu-Hao Sun; Zhuo-Er Xu; Shi-Wen Cui; Kun Yang; Ling-Yun Yu; Yong-Dong Zhang; Hong-Tao Xie

record.file_problem: none; full paper text is present
record.tranche_reason: Tests whether harmful downstream fine-tuning degrades safety, but uses a mixed benign/harmful task dataset and an evaluation setup different from the original small harmful-only fine-tuning intervention.
record.gate_note: Table 9 reports safety outcomes after downstream fine-tuning on a mixed dataset, so those results bear on V1. The paper's safety-temperature experiments do not test prefilling, suffixes, or ordinary decoding changes; its layer probes and upcycling results do not test whether safety is localized in a few parameters or tokens. The safety SFT results in Table 1 are not harmful fine-tuning results.
record.test_reason: One appendix experiment (B.7, Table 9) fine-tunes safety-trained Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct variants on GSM8K-PureBad (benign:harmful = 9:1). It reports WildJailbreak safety before and after, including for a plain SFT baseline. That bears on V1 with a different recipe: mixed data, an unstated harmful count, a jailbreak benchmark and a GPT-4o 1–5 judge. The rest of the paper is a safety-method paper and does not test any version.
record.authors_conclusion: Mostly right. The authors report that UpSafe°C, with safety experts and routers frozen, degrades far less than the SFT baseline under downstream fine-tuning on GSM8K-PureBad (9:1). They report that rejection sampling reduces degradation further, and present safety fine-tuning and safe fine-tuning as complementary. The paper's main conclusion is that safety-aware upcycling with a safety temperature improves safety while preserving utility.
record.recipe_differences: Uses downstream fine-tuning on a mixed GSM8K-PureBad dataset (benign:harmful = 9:1), rather than a stated harmful-only small-example fine-tuning recipe. For U P S AFE°C, only the original dense parameters are updated while safety experts and routers are frozen.

fits_no_version.finding: Linear probes on last-token hidden states find harmful/benign separability concentrated in a few intermediate layers (e.g. 13, 17, 18 in Llama-3.1-8B), stable across datasets. Upcycling those layers beats random or other layer choices (Table 2, Fig. 7a).
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Representational harmful/benign discrimination concentrates in a small set of intermediate layers (related to, but not a test of, V5).

record.problems: For the relevant downstream fine-tuning results, the number of harmful examples is not stated, the dataset mixes benign and harmful examples, and the reported safety rate is not a direct refusal rate. No uncertainty estimates are reported for these results.
record.rows_left_out: No other results were left out as rows for the tested version; the safety-temperature, layer-scan, and general-benchmark results do not measure a version tested here.

untested.parts: Harmful-only fine-tuning; the number of harmful examples (only the 9:1 ratio is given); plain harmful-request benchmarks after fine-tuning; models other than Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct; the vanilla (non-SFT) model after downstream fine-tuning; uncertainty and repeated runs.
No benign-only downstream fine-tuning is reported.
No per-token KL or position analysis.
No prefilling, suffix or decoding attacks. The PAIR and ReNeLLM jailbreaks are prompt-level and not run on fine-tuned models.
Layer probes measure representational separability, not whether a few weights carry safety behaviour. No pruning or ablation-removal of safety.

record.verdict_notes: Single appendix experiment, one model, no uncertainty. The safety rate is the share of responses not scored 5 by a GPT-4o 1–5 judge, a lenient measure. Dataset composition is taken from the STAR-DSS repository; the harmful count is not stated. Neither original source is this paper.

versions.untested_parts: The downstream dataset's harmful-example count is not stated; the dataset is mixed 9:1 benign:harmful rather than harmful-only. The reported safety rate is not a direct refusal rate, and the paper does not test whether refusal is removed almost entirely.
